alpha_potential: Potential for developing adaptive trading strategies that can adjust to changing market conditions, with theoretical guarantees on sample efficiency. The optimistic approach may help in exploration of profitable strategies in uncertain markets.
title_cn: 基于参数化策略的乐观行动者-评论家方法在线性马尔可夫决策过程中的应用
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种用于线性MDP的乐观行动者-评论家框架，采用参数化对数线性策略。通过logit匹配回归训练行动者，使用Langevin Monte Carlo近似Thompson采样训练评论家。该方法在理论上保证了样本效率，可应用于开发适应市场变化的量化交易策略，特别是在不确定市场环境中探索盈利机会。

title: Inverse Design for Conditional Distribution Matching
summary: Generative models are powerful tools for sampling from a learned distribution $\mathcal{P}(Y \mid X)$, and inverse-design methods invert this map to find an input $x$ that produces a desired point output $y^*$. However, many design goals are naturally distributional rather than pointwise, incorporating the inherent uncertainty of $Y$ and targeting a specific form for it, a task not addressed by standard inverse design. To address this issue we introduce Conditional Distribution Matching (CDM), a new inverse-design problem class in generative modeling: given a joint distribution $\mathcal{P}(X, Y)$ and a target distribution $\mathcal{G}(Y)$, find an input $x^*$ whose induced conditional distribution $\mathcal{P}(Y \mid X = x^*)$ matches $\mathcal{G}$. We formally define two variants: Conditional Distribution Matching Sampling (CDMS) and Conditional Distribution Matching Optimization (CDMO). To solve these problems, we propose MLGD-F (Matching-Loss Guided Diffusion with a Fast inner sampler), a plug-and-play inference-time algorithm that combines a pretrained score-based diffusion model with a pretrained fast conditional sampler, requiring no additional training or fine-tuning. By leveraging single-step conditional sampling, MLGD-F enables tractable gradient computation, making the estimation of $\mathcal{P}(Y \mid X)$ both memory-efficient and computationally lightweight. We validate MLGD-F on synthetic benchmarks, structured image transformations, and generative editing optimization, demonstrating reliable recovery of inputs whose conditional distributions match diverse user-specified targets, including discrete mixtures and continuous low-rank supports.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Conditional Distribution Matching (CDM) and proposes MLGD-F, an inference-time algorithm that combines a pretrained score-based diffusion model with a fast conditional sampler to match target distributions. This method enables efficient gradient computation and distribution matching without additional training.
data_sources: The paper validates the method on synthetic benchmarks, structured image transformations, and generative editing optimization, but does not specify financial data sources. However, the methodology could be adapted to financial time series or market data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be applied to generate or optimize trading strategies by matching desired return distributions, managing portfolio risk, or creating synthetic data for backtesting. The ability to match conditional distributions could help in scenarios where the goal is to achieve specific statistical properties in returns or risk metrics.
title_cn: 条件分布匹配的逆向设计
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种新的逆向设计方法——条件分布匹配（CDM），通过结合预训练的扩散模型和快速条件采样器，实现目标分布的高效匹配。该方法在金融领域可应用于生成符合特定统计特性的交易策略或优化投资组合风险分布，具有潜在的实际应用价值。

title: When Do Foundation Models Pay Off? A Break-Even Analysis of Pretrained Time Series Forecasters
summary: Deploying a time series foundation model (FM) requires GPU infrastructure and engineering overhead, with no guarantee of improvement over classical forecasting methods. We provide the first systematic break-even analysis of when this investment pays off. Across 30 benchmark datasets, we compare zero-shot and LoRA fine-tuned FMs (Chronos-Bolt, Moirai, Lag-Llama) against classical baselines (Naive, ETS, ARIMA, XGBoost) at six training set sizes from 2% to 100% of available data. FMs outperform classical methods at every evaluated training fraction on 16 of 30 datasets. On 6 datasets, classical methods surpass zero-shot FMs with at most 5% of the training data (21--6,324 samples); on the remaining 8, break-even ranges from 24 to 22,177 samples. No classical method dominates: ARIMA, Naive, ETS and XGBoost are each best on 6--11 datasets. One robust rule requires no model training: if n_train < 700 and seasonality is non-negligible, FM zero-shot is the right low-data choice -- below 20% of the history, classical methods either lose to it (4 of these 10 datasets) or cannot be fitted at all (6) -- and it stays best at full history on 6 of them; fine-tuning should be skipped. Contrary to common practice, LoRA fine-tuning rarely helps and degrades short series by up to 52%. We operationalise these findings as a two-step decision framework -- compute dataset length and seasonality strength, run a brief 5--10% pilot only if needed. Cheap dataset features do not predict the break-even category at this benchmark scale, so outside the rule a pilot remains necessary. Code and benchmark: https://github.com/nicolaisi/fm_breakeven.
core_methodology: Systematic comparison of time series foundation models (FMs) against classical forecasting methods across different training set sizes, with a focus on break-even analysis to determine when FMs outperform classical methods.
data_sources: 30 benchmark datasets, including various time series data, compared against classical baselines (Naive, ETS, ARIMA, XGBoost).
alpha_potential: The study provides actionable insights on when to use FMs for time series forecasting, which can be applied to financial time series prediction, potentially improving trading strategy performance by selecting the right model based on dataset characteristics.
title_cn: 基础模型何时值得投资？预训练时间序列预测器的盈亏平衡分析
summary_cn: 本研究通过系统比较时间序列基础模型（FMs）与传统方法在不同训练集大小下的表现，提供了何时使用FMs的盈亏平衡分析。研究发现，在短序列和显著季节性数据中，FM零样本表现最佳，而微调通常无益。这些发现可帮助量化交易者在选择时间序列预测模型时做出更优决策，尤其在数据有限或季节性强的场景中。

title: How do features act in an individual prediction? Separating standalone and interaction effects with a case-based taxonomy
summary: Local explanation methods such as SHAP and LIME summarize each feature with a single attribution score, and interaction indices quantify how strongly features interact. Neither tells a user how a feature acts in a given prediction: whether its effect is the same alone and in context, or whether the other features amplify it, make it unnecessary, switch it off or reverse it. We extend case-based feature importance (CBFI), originally a global method, to individual predictions. Evaluating the model in four hybrid states per background sample decomposes the in-context importance of a feature into a standalone and an interaction effect, and a case taxonomy labels each feature of an instance as inactive, standalone, amplified, redundant, gated or reversed. We compare the method with k-SII, TreeSHAP interaction values and the H-statistic on synthetic functions, and study eight real tabular datasets with six model families. On the true functions, the decomposition recovered interactions exactly (correlation 0.99 with the analytic local interaction). On fitted models, pair recovery was slightly below that of dedicated indices (local precision@k 0.86-0.91 versus 0.91-0.95). Interaction values alone could not distinguish substitution from gating, whereas the taxonomy identified both without knowing the partner (accuracy 0.74-0.76); applied to Shapley interaction values, it performed comparably. On real data, 45-57% of feature pairs with nearly identical SHAP values received different labels, and in a medical-insurance model the method showed that the interaction component of smoking changes sign at a body-mass index of 30. Localized CBFI does not detect interactions more accurately than existing indices; what it adds is a decomposition into standalone and interaction effects and a label stating how each feature acts.
core_methodology: Extends case-based feature importance (CBFI) to individual predictions by decomposing feature effects into standalone and interaction components, and categorizes features into six interaction types (inactive, standalone, amplified, redundant, gated, reversed).
data_sources: Tested on synthetic functions and eight real tabular datasets, including a medical-insurance model.
alpha_potential: Could enhance feature interpretation in trading models by identifying how features interact in specific market conditions, potentially uncovering nuanced signals that traditional SHAP/LIME methods miss. Particularly useful for analyzing non-linear relationships in factor models or regime-switching environments.
title_cn: 特征在个体预测中如何发挥作用？通过基于案例的分类法分离独立效应和交互效应
summary_cn: 该研究扩展了基于案例的特征重要性方法，可将预测中特征的独立效应与交互效应分离，并标注六种交互类型。在金融领域，该方法有助于识别市场不同状态下因子间的复杂交互模式（如动量因子与波动率因子的非线性关系），为改进交易策略的信号组合提供新视角。

title: IQS-BO: In-Context Query Selection for Bayesian Optimisation
summary: Bayesian Optimisation (BO) is a powerful framework for optimising expensive black-box functions, but typically requires refitting a surrogate and maximising an acquisition function at every evaluation. In-context approaches based on Prior-data Fitted Networks (PFNs) amortise part of this cost by pre-training transformers on functions drawn from synthetic priors. PFNS4BO amortises the surrogate but still relies on a numerically maximised acquisition function, while FIBO performs BO fully in-context by sampling optimiser locations from a learned density, which fixes the decision rule and admits no surrogate. Learned acquisition functions score a finite candidate set with a network, but, lacking a label for the query, learn the score by reinforcement learning. We propose IQS-BO, a PFN that learns the query decision by supervised learning on synthetic priors. In a single forward pass, IQS-BO predicts the probability that each candidate is the best in the set, and we show that training minimises its expected KL divergence to the posterior probability of this event. The model can be pre-trained without a surrogate for fully in-context BO, or take the predictions of a fixed probabilistic surrogate as additional input, amortising only the decision step. Our method proposes queries at a fraction of the cost of acquisition-based methods, while matching or outperforming BO with Gaussian processes (GPs) and available in-context methods in sequential and batch optimisation, in low and high dimensions. Finally, we propose a mixture prior for pre-training PFNs which combines samples from GPs with functions exhibiting warped inputs, narrow optima, or plateaus that are poorly modelled by stationary GP kernels. We show that pre-training on this prior can improve performance and help the network generalise to a broader range of optimisation problems.
core_methodology: IQS-BO is a Prior-data Fitted Network (PFN) that learns the query decision by supervised learning on synthetic priors, predicting the probability that each candidate is the best in the set. It can be pre-trained without a surrogate for fully in-context Bayesian Optimization (BO), or take the predictions of a fixed probabilistic surrogate as additional input.
data_sources: The method is tested on synthetic functions drawn from priors that combine samples from Gaussian Processes (GPs) with functions exhibiting warped inputs, narrow optima, or plateaus. Real-world applications could extend to financial time series or optimization problems in trading strategies.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to optimize trading strategies by selecting the best parameters or signals from a set of candidates efficiently, potentially reducing computational costs compared to traditional BO methods. However, direct application to financial markets would require validation on market data.
title_cn: IQS-BO：贝叶斯优化的上下文查询选择
summary_cn: IQS-BO是一种基于上下文学习的贝叶斯优化方法，通过监督学习在合成先验上预测候选集中最优解的概率。该方法可显著降低计算成本，适用于交易策略参数优化，但需在真实市场数据上验证其有效性。

title: Prescriptive Learning of Linear Policies with Feasibility Guarantees for Binary Decision-Making
summary: Binary decision-making under uncertainty arises across a wide range of applications, including energy systems scheduling, transportation, and workforce planning. While machine learning has been increasingly applied to accelerate or replace mixed-integer solvers in such settings, existing approaches rely on predictive learning, training models to reproduce optimal decisions from labeled data, which lacks knowledge of counterfactual outcomes and provides no guarantees that the resulting decisions will be feasible. This limitation is further compounded under distributional shift, where policies trained on historical data may produce systematically infeasible decisions. We propose a prescriptive learning framework for binary decision-making that addresses both limitations. Rather than predicting optimal labels, the framework jointly optimizes over linear decision policies and feasible assignments across all training scenarios, allowing feasible alternatives and their operational performance to be considered directly during training. We further extend the framework to a distributionally robust chance-constrained formulation using a Wasserstein ambiguity set, which enforces feasibility with a prescribed probability under the worst-case distribution in the ambiguity set and enables a tunable trade-off between robustness and solution quality. We demonstrate the framework on two case studies, namely a unit commitment problem and a staff allocation problem. Out-of-sample experiments under test distributions that either match or differ from the training distribution show that the robust model is more conservative when the two distributions coincide, while under distributional shift it substantially reduces unmet demand and lowers total cost by up to 76.5% relative to classical predictive learning.
core_methodology: A prescriptive learning framework for binary decision-making that jointly optimizes over linear decision policies and feasible assignments across all training scenarios. It includes a distributionally robust chance-constrained formulation using a Wasserstein ambiguity set to enforce feasibility under worst-case distributions.
data_sources: Historical data for training and testing, potentially including energy systems scheduling, transportation, and workforce planning scenarios.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to ensure feasible decisions under distributional shift could be adapted for trading strategies that require robustness to market regime changes, potentially reducing unmet demand and lowering costs in portfolio optimization or execution strategies.
title_cn: 具有可行性保证的二进制决策线性策略的规范性学习
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种规范性学习框架，用于在二进制决策中联合优化线性策略和可行性分配，并通过Wasserstein模糊集实现分布鲁棒的可行性保证。在量化交易中，该方法可应用于市场制度变化下的投资组合优化或执行策略，降低未满足需求并减少成本，尤其在市场分布偏移时表现更优。

title: Regularizing Treatment Leakage for LLM-based Uplift Estimation
summary: Large language models (LLMs) provide semantic features for uplift estimation, but treatment-revealing text can induce prediction shortcuts that do not transfer to deployment. We propose LLM-based Uplift Leakage Regularization (LULR) to address this risk. With the LLM encoder frozen, LULR penalizes dependence between the causal head's trainable shared representation and treatment while retaining separate outcome heads. The penalty uses a variational approximation to the contrastive log-ratio upper bound (CLUB) of mutual information, targeting treatment dependence rather than generic parameter shrinkage. Controlled proxy experiments provide exploratory evidence of improved ranking scores under injected treatment information relative to no regularization and the tested weight-decay setting. Structured-only benchmarks show modest, dataset-dependent effects. On an industrial pricing randomized controlled trial, mean offline lift@0.3 is 0.258 for LULR, compared with 0.106 for the same-backbone baseline. A separate one-week online A/B test of the complete deployed pricing policy records 5.45% higher sales volume and 1.91% higher gross merchandise value than the control arm. These short-term policy-level gains do not isolate the regularizer's effect.
core_methodology: The paper proposes LLM-based Uplift Leakage Regularization (LULR) to address treatment leakage in uplift estimation using large language models (LLMs). The method penalizes dependence between the causal head's shared representation and treatment while retaining separate outcome heads, using a variational approximation to the contrastive log-ratio upper bound (CLUB) of mutual information.
data_sources: The paper uses text data for uplift estimation, with specific applications tested on an industrial pricing randomized controlled trial and a one-week online A/B test.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted for financial applications where treatment effects (e.g., policy changes, market interventions) need to be estimated without leakage from treatment-revealing information. This could be useful in algorithmic trading for evaluating the impact of new trading strategies or market conditions.
title_cn: 基于大语言模型的提升估计中的处理泄漏正则化
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种基于大语言模型（LLM）的提升泄漏正则化方法（LULR），用于解决提升估计中的处理泄漏问题。通过惩罚因果头的可训练共享表示与处理之间的依赖性，同时保留单独的结果头，该方法在工业定价随机对照试验中显示出较好的离线提升效果。这一方法可潜在应用于金融领域，如评估新交易策略或市场条件的影响。

title: Think Once, Act Fast: Cost-Effective Recursive Self-Improvement for Decision Model Harness
summary: Fast System-1 models enable responsive actions but struggle with complex or unfamiliar tasks. Large language model (LLM)-based System-2 provides strong reasoning capabilities, yet repeated invocation incurs substantial latency and computational costs. To bridge this gap, we propose JevRSI, a System-1/System-2 collaboration framework that transforms LLM reasoning into transferable decision support through recursive harness improvement. A Jev-style System-1 model enables low-latency action selection, while an asynchronous System-2 LLM develops a modular harness. The harness integrates procedures, state memory, and world models to provide decision contexts spanning the past, present, and future. Utility-driven retrieval selects modules based on both contextual relevance and their utility on previous tasks. Environmental feedback guides targeted revisions and enables recursive self-improvement. Experiments across three datasets show that JevRSI consistently improves decision quality, matching or surpassing LLM agents in several settings. It preserves low-latency execution with favorable performance-cost trade-offs. Moreover, System-2 development interventions decrease as the harness evolves, amortizing System-2 costs through continuous improvement. Our project is available at https://github.com/usail-hkust/JevRSI.
core_methodology: A hybrid System-1/System-2 framework where a fast System-1 model handles low-latency decisions while an LLM-based System-2 asynchronously develops and improves a modular decision harness with utility-driven retrieval and environmental feedback for recursive self-improvement.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be general decision-making tasks (could be adapted for market data)
alpha_potential: Potential for creating adaptive trading systems that combine fast execution with sophisticated reasoning, particularly in scenarios requiring rapid response to new information with complex contextual analysis.
title_cn: 快速思考，立即行动：决策模型框架的高性价比递归自我改进方法
summary_cn: JevRSI框架通过结合快速响应的System-1模型和LLM驱动的System-2推理系统，为量化交易提供了一种新型决策架构。其核心价值在于：1) 保持低延迟执行的同时提升复杂情境决策质量；2) 通过模块化决策框架实现经验积累和递归改进；3) 效用驱动的模块选择机制可适配不同市场状态。该技术特别适合需要快速响应与深度分析结合的高频交易或事件驱动策略。

title: Targeted Synthetic Control Method
summary: The synthetic control method (SCM) estimates causal effects in panel data with a single-treated unit by constructing a counterfactual outcome as a weighted combination of untreated control units that matches the pre-treatment trajectory. In this paper, we introduce the targeted synthetic control (TSC) method, a new two-stage estimator that directly estimates the counterfactual outcome. Specifically, our TSC method (1) yields a targeted debiasing estimator, in the sense that the targeted updating refines the initial weights to produce more stable weights; and (2) ensures that the final counterfactual estimation is a convex combination of observed control outcomes to enable direct interpretation of the synthetic control weights. TSC is flexible and can be instantiated with arbitrary machine learning models. Methodologically, TSC starts from an initial set of synthetic-control weights via a one-dimensional targeted update through the weight-tilting submodel, which calibrates the weights to reduce bias of weights estimation arising from pre-treatment fit. Furthermore, TSC avoids key shortcomings of existing methods (e.g., the augmented SCM), which can produce unbounded counterfactual estimates. Across extensive synthetic and real-world experiments, TSC consistently improves estimation accuracy over state-of-the-art SCM baselines.
core_methodology: The Targeted Synthetic Control (TSC) method is a two-stage estimator that constructs a counterfactual outcome by refining initial synthetic control weights through a targeted debiasing process. It ensures the final estimation is a convex combination of observed control outcomes, improving stability and interpretability of the weights.
data_sources: Panel data with a single-treated unit and multiple untreated control units, which can be adapted to financial time series data for event studies or impact analysis.
alpha_potential: The TSC method could be useful for estimating the causal impact of financial events (e.g., policy changes, corporate actions) by constructing more accurate counterfactuals. This may help in developing event-driven strategies or improving factor timing models.
title_cn: 目标合成控制方法
summary_cn: 目标合成控制（TSC）方法通过两阶段估计器改进传统合成控制方法，利用权重倾斜子模型进行针对性去偏，生成更稳定的反事实估计。在量化金融中，该方法可用于更准确地评估政策变化或公司事件对资产价格的影响，为事件驱动策略提供更可靠的因果效应估计。

title: Markets for Compute and Inference: Structure, Financing, and Risk Transfer
summary: Capacity to run large language models is rented by the accelerator-hour, and their output is sold by the million tokens. Both goods now have published price indices, an over-the-counter forward has traded on one, compute futures are listed offshore, and CME and ICE have specified futures on rental indices that await the United States regulator. We ask what in these two markets can be hedged, by whom, and at what price. Three findings stand out. First, the price that exchange contracts settle on is not the price that drives operators' revenue. The contracts on CME and ICE reference published short-dated rental rates, while most revenue, and with it credit quality, comes from private multi-year contracts whose prices are largely undisclosed. Second, the token price and the rental rate are linked by an identity through throughput and margin, but they are different exposures, so a hedge on the rental rate does not hedge the cost of inference; at the measured capability of GPT-5 the cheapest list price fell by a factor of 17 in twelve months, and by far less at lower capability. Third, the demand for hedging already sits in credit agreements, as the years by which operators' debt outlives their contracted revenue. Filings cannot measure that gap, because debt is scheduled year by year while contracted revenue rarely is, and the one loan that prices it settles the risk by cash prepayment against a model only the parties see. We design a reverse convertible note through which leveraged operators could buy protection against falling rental rates. Its coupon depends steeply on the annualised volatility of the rental rate, which the two public indices put between about 5% and 89% according to how each is built and the horizon measured; across that range the fair one-year coupon runs from 4.1% to 31.6%.
core_methodology: The paper analyzes the structure and hedging mechanisms in markets for compute and inference, focusing on the relationship between token prices and rental rates for large language models. It proposes financial instruments like reverse convertible notes for hedging against rental rate volatility.
data_sources: Published price indices for accelerator-hours and token outputs, over-the-counter forwards, compute futures, and rental indices from CME and ICE.
alpha_potential: Potential alpha could be derived from understanding and exploiting the price discrepancies between short-dated rental rates and multi-year contracts, as well as the volatility in rental rates and token prices. The proposed reverse convertible note could offer a new hedging strategy for leveraged operators.
title_cn: 计算与推理市场：结构、融资与风险转移
summary_cn: 本文分析了大型语言模型的计算能力和推理输出的市场结构，探讨了代币价格与租赁费率之间的关系，并提出了针对租赁费率波动的对冲工具。研究发现公开合约结算价格与运营商收入驱动价格存在差异，并提出了一种反向可转换票据作为对冲工具。

title: Dynamic Scenario-Based Portfolio Optimization for Multi-Asset ETFs
summary: Portfolio outcomes may depend as much on trading restrictions as on how returns are modeled. We compared historical moving-window returns with conditional scenarios from ARMA--GARCH models and a Student-$t$ copula for 30 U.S.-listed exchange-traded funds. Matched mean--variance and conditional value-at-risk portfolios were evaluated under long-only and limited long--short bounds over 946 sessions. Historical portfolios had higher observed reward--risk ratios in most comparisons, but no paired difference remained significant after multiple-testing adjustment. Conditional scenarios did not consistently reduce realized downside risk. We distinguished changes in target weights from trades required to rebalance holdings after market movements. Relaxing the target-adjustment limit changed exposures, turnover, and some returns more than varying scenario count or seed in the examined tests. These findings suggest that assessments of conditional return inputs should consider portfolio constraints and trading requirements.
core_methodology: The paper compares historical moving-window returns with conditional scenarios from ARMA-GARCH models and a Student-t copula for portfolio optimization. It evaluates mean-variance and conditional value-at-risk portfolios under different trading constraints.
data_sources: 30 U.S.-listed exchange-traded funds (ETFs) over 946 trading sessions.
alpha_potential: The study suggests that portfolio constraints and trading requirements may have more impact on outcomes than the choice of return modeling, indicating potential alpha in optimizing trading rules rather than just return predictions.
title_cn: 多资产ETF的动态情景投资组合优化
summary_cn: 本研究比较了历史移动窗口回报与ARMA-GARCH模型和Student-t copula生成的条件情景在投资组合优化中的表现。通过对30只美国上市ETF的946个交易日数据进行测试，发现投资组合约束和交易规则对结果的影响可能大于回报建模方法的选择。这一发现对量化交易中投资组合再平衡策略的优化具有实际指导意义。

title: DuoCL: Dual-Path Online Continual Learning
summary: Online continual learning (OCL) requires learning from a data stream whose arrival rate is independent of model training speed. When training cannot keep pace, computationally expensive gradient-based methods update less frequently, limiting adaptation. Analytic methods reduce this overhead, but their frozen backbones cannot adapt representations to changing distributions. We propose DuoCL, a dual-path OCL framework whose fast analytic path accumulates feature statistics from every incoming minibatch while its slow path periodically adapts the backbone. The slow path adjusts its sample count to the available compute budget without interrupting fast-path learning. Feature alignment compensates for drift in the accumulated classifier statistics. Across four datasets and three computational budgets, DuoCL improves online accuracy by an average of 9.67 percentage points over the strongest gradient-based baseline in each setting. DuoCL consistently outperforms analytic learning under distribution shifts, with gains of up to 4.00 percentage points on CIFAR-C, and achieves higher accuracy than prior methods across disjoint class-incremental, domain-incremental, and Si-Blurry settings.
core_methodology: Dual-path online continual learning framework combining fast analytic path for feature statistics accumulation and slow path for periodic backbone adaptation
data_sources: Tested on general image datasets (CIFAR-C and others), not financial data
alpha_potential: Potential adaptation for high-frequency trading scenarios where data distribution shifts rapidly, but requires significant domain adaptation
title_cn: DuoCL：双路径在线持续学习
summary_cn: 该论文提出的双路径持续学习框架在数据分布变化时能保持高准确率，理论上可适用于金融市场数据流快速变化的场景，如高频交易。但需要重新设计针对金融时间序列的特征提取和适应机制。

title: MINT: Meeting-time Indicators for Truncation in Multi-Step Off-Policy RL
summary: Many multi-step off-policy temporal-difference methods handle policy mismatch through products of per-step trace coefficients, leading to a trade-off between variance control and long-horizon signal. The maximum trace length consequently becomes a sensitive hyperparameter. We propose MINT (Meeting-time INdicators for Truncation), which replaces these products with a binary stopping indicator: one until coupled behavior and target trajectories first meet, zero thereafter. At the true value function, the indicator's idempotence yields a variance bound governed by meeting-time survival. For practical implementation, a single sampled action provides a model-free surrogate for the stopping rule, requiring no transition model or mixing-time estimate. We derive separate sufficient conditions for contraction of the state-coupled operator and its practical surrogate under fixed-policy evaluation. On MuJoCo and DeepMind Control tasks, MINT outperforms the reported multi-step baselines; the main MuJoCo comparison uses a common cap without per-task cap-length tuning. We also demonstrate the effectiveness of MINT on Atari 100k, RWRL, and OGBench experiments; MINT adapts the backup horizon to reduce target variability relative to long fixed-horizon backups across tasks and dynamics.
core_methodology: MINT introduces a multi-step off-policy reinforcement learning (RL) method that replaces traditional products of per-step trace coefficients with a binary stopping indicator, which activates until the behavior and target trajectories first meet. This approach aims to reduce variance and improve long-horizon signal capture.
data_sources: MuJoCo, DeepMind Control tasks, Atari 100k, RWRL, and OGBench experiments. These are simulation environments, but the methodology could theoretically be applied to financial time-series data.
alpha_potential: The method may provide a framework for developing trading strategies that adapt the prediction horizon dynamically, potentially better capturing market regimes or reducing variance compared to fixed-horizon backups.
title_cn: MINT：多步离策略强化学习中截断的会合时间指标
summary_cn: MINT提出一种改进的多步离策略强化学习方法，通过会合点停止指标动态调整预测周期长度。对于量化交易而言，该方法可能有助于降低波动并捕捉长周期市场信号，适合开发自适应市场状态的交易策略。

title: DyNA-Mixer: Decoupling Time and Topology for Scalable Dynamic Node Affinity Prediction
summary: Continuous-time dynamic graphs preserve the ordering, timing, and evolving strength of interactions that static snapshots discard, making dynamic graph mining essential for evolving systems such as recommender systems, trade networks, and transaction platforms. Research in this area has centered on dynamic link prediction, which forecasts only whether a future interaction will occur, whereas many applications also need its intensity. The dynamic node affinity prediction (DNAP) problem generalizes this task to continuous targets and full-candidate ranking, making it more broadly applicable but substantially harder. This raises two coupled difficulties: ranking requires a predictor expressive enough to capture both multi-scale temporal evolution and graph-wide collaborative patterns, yet running such a predictor over every source--destination pair is computationally prohibitive. We propose DyNA-Mixer, which decouples temporal forecasting from collaborative structure modeling. It adopts a multi-scale temporal predictor for pair-specific affinity evolution, constructs a Virtual Collaborative Graph that infers query-time relationships and aggregates trends from related interactions, and fuses the two through a gated residual mechanism. A sparsity-aware evaluation strategy further restricts expensive forecasting to pairs with recent non-zero affinities. Experiments on four Temporal Graph Benchmark datasets for the DNAP problem show that DyNA-Mixer achieves new state-of-the-art NDCG@10 on every dataset, including a 17.8\% relative test improvement over the strongest baseline on tgbn-token, the largest dataset.
core_methodology: DyNA-Mixer decouples temporal forecasting from collaborative structure modeling in dynamic graphs, using a multi-scale temporal predictor for pair-specific affinity evolution and a Virtual Collaborative Graph for query-time relationship inference and trend aggregation.
data_sources: Datasets from Temporal Graph Benchmark, applicable to transaction platforms and trade networks.
alpha_potential: Potential for modeling dynamic relationships in financial transaction networks, especially in high-frequency trading and order book dynamics, though the direct financial application is not explicitly demonstrated.
title_cn: DyNA-Mixer：通过解耦时间和拓扑实现可扩展的动态节点亲和度预测
summary_cn: DyNA-Mixer 通过解耦时间序列预测和协同结构建模，提高了动态图中节点亲和度预测的准确性和可扩展性，适用于金融交易网络中的动态关系建模和高频交易策略。

title: Loss-Controlling Calibration with Asymptotic Guarantees
summary: We propose a learning framework for calibrating predictive models to perform loss-controlling prediction, which extends our proposed conformal loss-controlling prediction framework to more general settings. In contrast to existing methods, the predictors built by the proposed approach are not restricted to set-valued predictors, and the loss function can be any measurable function without requiring monotonicity assumptions. The approach is a natural extension of conformal loss-controlling prediction, since it reduces to the latter when the predictors are set-valued with the nesting property and the losses are monotone. The loss-controlling guarantee of the proposed framework is established in the asymptotic setting and is empirically verified in selective regression and high-impact weather forecasting, demonstrating its effectiveness for the domains requiring general loss-controlling prediction.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a learning framework for calibrating predictive models to perform loss-controlling prediction, extending conformal loss-controlling prediction to more general settings. It allows for non-set-valued predictors and any measurable loss function without monotonicity requirements.
data_sources: The abstract mentions empirical verification in selective regression and high-impact weather forecasting, but does not specify financial data sources. In QF applications, this would likely use standard market data (prices, volumes) or alternative data streams.
alpha_potential: Potential application in risk management (controlling downside) and prediction confidence calibration for trading signals. Could help optimize tradeoff between prediction accuracy and risk exposure in algorithmic strategies.
title_cn: 具有渐近保证的损失控制校准
summary_cn: 本研究提出的损失控制预测校准框架可扩展应用于金融预测模型的误差控制。通过非单调损失函数的灵活处理能力，该技术有望优化交易信号的置信度校准，在控制投资组合下行风险方面具有应用潜力。校准后的模型可以更精确地平衡预测准确性与风险暴露。

title: Pragmatic Curiosity: A Unified Framework for Hybrid Learning and Optimization via Active Inference
summary: Many engineering and scientific workflows rely on expensive black-box evaluations, requiring sequential decisions that must both improve task performance and reduce uncertainty. Bayesian optimization (BO) and Bayesian experimental design (BED) provide powerful but largely separate treatments of goal-directed optimization and information-seeking experimentation, leaving limited guidance for hybrid settings in which learning and optimization are intrinsically coupled. We propose Pragmatic Curiosity (PraC), a unified framework for hybrid learning and optimization via active inference. PraC evaluates candidate queries by trading information gain about a task-relevant latent symbol against an expected regret-based potential over outcomes. This formulation foregrounds three operational design choices: which latent quantity should be clarified, how task value is encoded as regret, and how strongly information gain should be exchanged against pragmatic regret. We instantiate PraC across three regimes of increasing complexity: decision-oriented monitoring with fixed global symbols and known downstream losses, targeted active search with induced local symbols and evolving coverage goals, and composite Bayesian optimization with hierarchical regret learning under unknown preferences. Across these regimes, PraC reduces downstream decision risk, improves coverage of critical outcome regions, and jointly learns predictive and preference structures without relying on task-specific staging rules.
core_methodology: The paper presents Pragmatic Curiosity (PraC), a unified framework that combines Bayesian optimization (BO) and Bayesian experimental design (BED) to balance between goal-directed optimization and information-seeking exploration. It introduces a novel approach to active inference for hybrid learning and optimization by trading off information gain about latent task-relevant symbols against expected regret-based potential over outcomes.
data_sources: The abstract does not explicitly mention specific financial market data, but the methodology can be applied to various quantitative finance problems requiring sequential decision-making under uncertainty, such as portfolio optimization, derivatives pricing, or algorithmic trading strategy development.
alpha_potential: The framework has potential for uncovering alpha through better sequential decision-making in financial applications where learning and optimization need to be balanced. It could help in designing more robust trading strategies that dynamically adjust based on new information and changing market conditions, potentially reducing regret in trading decisions.
title_cn: 实用好奇心：通过主动推理实现混合学习与优化的统一框架
summary_cn: 该论文提出了'实用好奇心'(PraC)框架，将贝叶斯优化与实验设计相结合，通过主动推理平衡学习与优化。在量化交易中可应用于动态投资组合优化和算法交易策略的开发，帮助交易系统在不确定市场环境下更好地权衡信息获取与决策优化，潜在降低交易决策中的遗憾值。框架支持从已知损失函数到未知偏好的多层次优化场景。

title: Pareto-Informed Smart "Predict, then Optimize" for Multi-Objective Combinatorial Problems
summary: Many real-world planning applications, from logistics, routing to resource allocation, give rise to optimization problems that need to balance multiple, conflicting objectives. While machine learning is often used to predict the unknown parameters or costs of these problems, standard models trained on prediction accuracy can lead to suboptimal plans. Decision-Focused Learning (DFL) addresses this by integrating the downstream optimization task into the training objective. However, existing DFL methods for multi-objective problems rely on simple scalarization, which fails to capture the rich trade-offs of the Pareto Frontier. To address this gap, we propose a Pareto-aware extension to single-objective Smart "Predict, then Optimize" (SPO+) for multi-objective combinatorial optimization problems. Our loss function leverages the true Pareto Frontier, forming a target decision that aligns with a sampled preference vector, and minimizes regret against this target. Experiments on multi-objective shortest path and multi-objective knapsack problems show that our approach outperforms traditional two-stage Mean Squared Error (MSE) baselines. It also surpasses scalarization-based SPO+ approaches.
core_methodology: Pareto-informed Decision-Focused Learning (DFL) for multi-objective optimization problems, leveraging the true Pareto Frontier to align predictions with optimization goals and minimize regret against a target decision.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned in abstract (typically requires problem-specific parameters like costs, weights, or constraints in combinatorial problems).
alpha_potential: Potential application in portfolio optimization where multiple conflicting objectives (return, risk, liquidity) must be balanced, potentially generating more efficient frontiers than scalarization-based methods.
title_cn: 多目标组合问题的帕累托智能'预测后优化'方法
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种基于帕累托前沿的多目标决策优化方法，通过将真实帕累托解融入损失函数来优化预测与决策的一致性。在交易领域可应用于多目标投资组合优化，比传统标量化方法更有效平衡收益与风险等冲突目标。

title: Tracking Representations in LLM Reasoning Traces for Iterated Games
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents achieve state-of-the-art performance across domains through chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning. Despite their ubiquitous use, little is understood about the relationship between the externalized trace and the model's actual computation. We address this by investigating how LLM agents make decisions in iterative games with incomplete information. Using a series of mechanistic interpretability techniques, we find that the model forms and iteratively revises an internal representation of the game throughout the CoT. Once the model prematurely commits to an incorrect belief, it rarely recovers. This failure is manifested in both the literal trace and the layer activations. Ultimately, as multi-agent systems are more prevalent, our work opens the door to a more focused diagnosis of their strategic reasoning errors. For illustrative purposes, we offer an interactive visualizer of our methodology on selected sample traces at https://interp-self.github.io/gametrace/
core_methodology: Mechanistic interpretability techniques to analyze LLM decision-making in iterative games with incomplete information
data_sources: Not specified (theoretical study using simulated interactive games)
alpha_potential: Limited - provides insights into LLM reasoning failures but no clear market application

title: Entropy-Regularized Integrated Gradients for Stable Feature Attribution
summary: Path-based attribution methods like Integrated Gradients (IG) are widely used to interpret neural networks, yet imperceptible input perturbations can drastically alter their attribution maps while leaving model predictions unchanged. We introduce Entropy-Regularized Integrated Gradients (ERIG), a path-based attribution method that intrinsically attenuates gradient irregularities along the integration path using maximum-entropy softmax weighting with temperature parameter $\tau$. We quantify the effect of the entropy-regularized weighting on attribution stability by using the Lipschitz properties of the model and its gradients. We decompose the attribution change under an input perturbation into a model-response term, whose bound is $\tau$-independent, and a weight-variation term, whose bound decreases at rate $\mathcal{O}(1/(2\tau))$. Their ratio $R(\tau)$ characterizes the trade-off between gradient information and attribution stability. We further add a new dimension to attribution evaluation by adapting classical noise estimators into two metrics, LINV-C and LINV-P, that quantify attribution noise. Across eleven CNN and Transformer backbones on ImageNet and Oxford-IIIT Pet datasets, our experiments show that, relative to the next-best method, ERIG remains comparable on ranking-based fidelity metrics while improving localization by approximately 24% and attribution stability by approximately 47-fold on average, reaching up to four orders of magnitude improvement over IG, all at negligible additional computational cost.
core_methodology: Entropy-regularized path-based attribution method for neural network interpretability
data_sources: ImageNet and Oxford-IIIT Pet datasets (computer vision)
alpha_potential: Potential for improving model interpretability in financial ML models, but no direct trading application demonstrated

title: When Normal-Only Updates Are Not Enough: Test-Time Adaptation in Reconstruction-Based Time-Series Anomaly Detection
summary: Normal operating conditions can evolve after deployment, motivating test-time adaptation (TTA) of time-series anomaly detectors using incoming data. Yet the same stream may contain anomalies, so TTA with online updates must decide which test samples should be used for adaptation. This leaves a more basic question: even if updates are restricted to samples labeled as normal in the benchmark, does TTA reliably improve anomaly detection? We study this question with a controlled intervention that replaces the practical update selector with a rule that uses only samples labeled as normal in the benchmark, while keeping the rest of the online adaptation procedure unchanged. Across nine benchmark families, four optimizer configurations, and five random seeds, we obtain three main findings: (1) using only samples labeled as normal in the benchmark does not reliably improve detection; (2) practical TTA failures exhibit two distinct responses to this intervention, with 63 of 180 settings recovering a clear detection gain while 90 still show no clear detection gain; and (3) the updates reduce their immediate reconstruction objective across the evaluated settings, yet these reductions do not consistently lead to better anomaly ranking. Both failure patterns persist across alternative practical adaptation variants and modest perturbations of the benchmark labels. Together, these findings show that improving sample selection alone is not a complete solution to reconstruction-based TSAD TTA.
core_methodology: Test-time adaptation (TTA) for time-series anomaly detection, focusing on reconstruction-based methods and the impact of using only normal-labeled samples for updates
data_sources: Time-series data from nine benchmark families, with labels indicating normal and anomalous samples
alpha_potential: Limited direct alpha potential; the study highlights challenges in adapting anomaly detection models to evolving conditions, which could indirectly inform risk management or outlier detection in financial time series

title: A Mechanistic Analysis of In-Context Learning and Out-of-Context Hallucination
summary: Large language models can infer and follow specific rules through in-context learning (ICL), yet may fail to remain faithful to provided evidence, giving rise to out-of-context (OOC) hallucination. Existing work has largely investigated the underlying mechanisms of ICL and OOC hallucination along separate lines. However, this separation obscures the mechanistic basis for these seemingly opposing outcomes. In this work, we study this contrast through the unified view of functional roles in dynamic context. The key observation is that role information can be internally represented without reliably constraining output. We derive a first-order decomposition to characterize the role effect, showing that its substantial influence depends on two necessary conditions, namely sufficient contribution magnitude and coherent signed aggregation. Causal analysis further shows that role span contributions affect key token choices involving response structure, content selection, and factual values. We further show that role-consistent choices depend on sufficient role span support at these key decisions, while failing choices can be reversed when this support overcomes the deficit. These findings support a common mechanistic view of ICL and OOC hallucination: each functional role defines the pattern of output decisions over which role span contributions must remain effective, and differences in this organization account for the seemingly opposing outcomes.
core_methodology: Mechanistic analysis of in-context learning and out-of-context hallucination in large language models
data_sources: Not specified (theoretical analysis of LLM behavior)
alpha_potential: Potential insights for improving LLM reliability in financial document analysis, but no direct trading application demonstrated

title: Learning with Unlearning: Synaptic Role Partitioning for Simultaneous Continual Learning and Machine Unlearning
summary: Continual Learning (CL) asks a model to acquire new knowledge without forgetting what it already knows. Machine Unlearning (MU) asks it to destroy specific knowledge without damaging the rest. The challenge is integrating them in the same system; the two objectives pull on the same weights, and an edit made for one harms the other. To address this, we propose Learning with Unlearning (LwU), a unified framework that resolves the conflict where it occurs: at the individual synapse. LwU scores every weight twice, once against the data to keep and once against the data to delete, and partitions the network into four zones with separate update rules. Weights that only require retention are frozen. Weights that only require deletion are cleared and returned to the network as free capacity. Contested weights take a gradient-ascent step projected orthogonally to the retention gradient. The remaining capacity learns the incoming task by a privileged teacher via self-distillation. Deletion is served post hoc, and no retraining is required. Across both CL and MU jobs, LwU outperforms or matches the strongest baseline. Its real-world practicality has been demonstrated on the Physical Artificial Intelligence (PAI) dataset we conducted. Additionally, in the image generation task and in removing dangerous content, it outperformed the closest baseline, as shown in Fig.1.
core_methodology: A unified framework (LwU) that partitions neural network weights into four zones with separate update rules to handle both continual learning and machine unlearning simultaneously.
data_sources: Physical Artificial Intelligence (PAI) dataset, image generation tasks, and content removal tasks.
alpha_potential: Potential for adaptive model updating in dynamic financial environments, but direct application to trading strategies is unclear.

title: Towards Reliable Scaling Laws for Tabular Foundation Models
summary: Scaling laws are widely used to predict foundation model performance and guide compute allocation. However, tabular foundation models (TFMs) differ from conventional foundation models in that they are pretrained on virtually unlimited synthetic data from configurable distributions, while ultimately being evaluated on real-world datasets. We investigate whether scaling laws for TabPFNv2-style models reliably extrapolate to larger compute budgets and generalize across evaluation settings. Our analysis reveals differences between synthetic and real-world scaling behavior and shows that accurately fitting a scaling law does not necessarily yield reliable prescriptions on unseen datasets. In particular, selecting configurations using too few evaluation datasets leads to systematically over-optimistic performance estimates. We further demonstrate that compute-optimal scaling requires expanding the range of synthetic pretraining dataset sizes alongside model size and training compute. Increasing the maximum numbers of rows and features sampled during pretraining improves performance and produces more predictable scaling trends. These insights guide the training of more efficient TabPFNv2-like models, using the open-source training pipeline of nanoTabPFN.
core_methodology: Investigates scaling laws for tabular foundation models (TFMs) pretrained on synthetic data and evaluated on real-world datasets
data_sources: Synthetic tabular data and real-world datasets (unspecified financial relevance)
alpha_potential: Potential for improving model efficiency in tabular data processing, but direct financial application unclear

title: VAFL: A Vertical Analytic Federated Learning Mechanism for Efficient Crowdsourced Services via Closed-Form Solutions
summary: Intelligent services often rely on complementary information held by different organizations, motivating Vertical Federated Learning without centralized raw-data pooling. We propose VAFL, a Vertical Analytic Federated Learning framework that fits classification and regression heads on fixed local representations through regularized least squares. An agent-assisted protected-computation workflow supports two-party and multi-party collaboration. To reduce fitting overhead, we develop a full-dimensional equivalent solve that applies block factors directly to the target matrix, avoiding construction of the full inverse. We further study two width-reduction strategies: local spectral projection with coefficient lifting, and full-dimensional local fitting with low-rank cross-party correction. The first compresses the prediction space, whereas the second retains local components outside the collaboration subspace. We establish their algebraic properties and analyze their computational scope. Experiments on five benchmarks show the accuracy--cost tradeoffs of these strategies and compatibility with diverse frozen backbones. Predictive performance and training time identify useful operating points and the limits of compression.
core_methodology: Vertical Federated Learning framework for classification and regression using regularized least squares
data_sources: Complementary information from different organizations (not explicitly financial data)
alpha_potential: Potential for privacy-preserving multi-party data collaboration, but no clear connection to market inefficiencies or trading signals

title: How Generative Models Generate: A Concise Guide to the Generative AI Landscape
summary: The rapidly expanding generative AI landscape brings together methods that differ in architecture, learning objective, mathematical representation and sampling procedure. A concise, selectively organised technical guide can provide an accessible starting point for developing a coherent understanding of this increasingly complex landscape. This article takes a generation-centred approach, connecting how models produce new observations with the modelling and learning principles that make generation possible. We develop a two-level perspective: first, distinguishing three recurring generation routes-direct transformation or decoding, sequential conditional construction, and iterative updating or transport; and second, examining the modelling and learning principles underlying these routes. Representative approaches are introduced through their key components, learning objectives and sampling procedures. We then examine their broader connections, including how different architectures and generation mechanisms can overlap or be combined. By bringing together essential technical explanations within a compact conceptual framework, the article aims to help readers develop a working understanding of unfamiliar approaches, recognise connections among models they have encountered, and navigate different approaches within the broader generative AI landscape.
core_methodology: The paper provides a conceptual framework for understanding different generative AI approaches, focusing on three generation routes: direct transformation, sequential conditional construction, and iterative updating.
data_sources: Not applicable (theoretical paper)
alpha_potential: Limited direct alpha potential, but could inform the development of generative models for synthetic data generation or scenario analysis in trading.

title: On-Policy Morphing into Hybrid Attention Models
summary: Hybrid attention models combine full and linear attention to achieve a better quality--efficiency trade-off. Converting pretrained Transformers into such models requires identifying which layers should retain full attention under a prescribed budget. We identify two off-policy mismatches in FlashMorph's layer selection: (i) continuous branch interpolation and teacher-forced hidden states differ from discrete hybrid computation; and (ii) frozen model weights fail to account for parameter adaptation during subsequent recovery. We introduce FlashMorph2, an on-policy layer-selection method that (I) evaluates sampled discrete hybrid architectures end to end using their own hidden states, and (II) jointly optimizes layer-selection scores and model weights under the recovery objective to reflect post-adaptation performance. Experiments across Qwen3 model scales and linear-attention variants show that FlashMorph2 consistently outperforms existing layer-selection methods, improving average scores over FlashMorph by $+2.42$ points on RULER, $+1.08$ on LongBench, and $+0.76$ on recall-intensive tasks, while completing layer selection in only $0.72$--$3.57$ GPU hours across 0.6B--8B models, demonstrating high efficiency and scalability.
core_methodology: Hybrid attention models combining full and linear attention to optimize quality-efficiency trade-off in Transformers
data_sources: General model evaluation datasets (RULER, LongBench, recall-intensive tasks)
alpha_potential: Potential indirect value in improving efficiency of transformer-based models that could later be applied to financial data processing, but no direct trading application demonstrated

title: Improved Leverage Score Sampling for Constrained Active Linear Regression
summary: In this paper we study active learning for constrained linear regression. Given a design matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$, a constraint set $C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$, and query access to $b\in\mathbb{R}^n$, we seek an approximate solution to $\min_{x\in C}\|Ax-b\|_2^2$ using as few queries as possible. This problem arises in many scientific and engineering applications, and randomized leverage score sampling provides a powerful method to solve it. However, existing leverage score methods ignore the constraint or encode it through ridge regularization, suffering unfavorable query complexity for anisotropic constraint sets. We propose ellipsoid-regularized leverage scores, where we approximate the constraint set by an outer ellipsoid and use its shape matrix to bias sampling toward directions that matter under the constraint geometry. We prove that the query complexity is governed by an anisotropic effective dimension $d_{\text{eff}}(C)\le d$. With appropriate parameters, $O(d_{\text{eff}}(C)\log d/\varepsilon^2)$ queries suffice to return a point in $C$ with objective value at most $(1+\varepsilon)$ times the optimum. This bound can substantially improve on the standard leverage-score bound, since anisotropic constraints can make $d_{\text{eff}}(C)$ much smaller than $d$. For convex constraints, we improve the dependence on $\varepsilon$ from $1/\varepsilon^2$ to $1/\varepsilon$. We also prove two lower bounds: first, the $d/\varepsilon^2$ dependence is unavoidable without convexity assumptions on $C$, and second, in some regimes, the effective dimension dependence $d_{\mathrm{eff}}(C)/\varepsilon$ is necessary for ellipsoidal constraints. Experiments on synthetic regression problems and a parametric heat conduction problem show lower regression error than standard baselines for similar query budget.
core_methodology: Active learning with ellipsoid-regularized leverage scores for constrained linear regression
data_sources: Synthetic regression problems and parametric heat conduction data (not financial datasets)
alpha_potential: Limited direct applicability - methodology might theoretically improve portfolio optimization with constraints, but no demonstrated financial applications

title: AG-BFGS: Foundations for Accelerated Geometry Learning
summary: We introduce an accelerated geometry-learning framework for BFGS that incorporates momentum into the learning of Hessian inverse approximations. We prove that the resulting accelerated updates satisfy explicit stability conditions and preserve positive definiteness within admissible parameter regions. Numerical experiments demonstrate consistent improvements over the corresponding non-accelerated schemes while maintaining numerical stability. These results provide the first rigorous theoretical foundation for accelerated quasi-Newton learning and bridge the gap between empirical observations and mathematical guarantees for accelerated second-order methods.
core_methodology: Accelerated BFGS method with momentum incorporated into Hessian inverse approximations
data_sources: Numerical experiments (no specific financial data mentioned)
alpha_potential: Potential for improving portfolio optimization through enhanced second-order optimization

title: Functional Principal Component Analysis: Minimax Optimality from Sparse to Dense Designs and Beyond
summary: Functional principal component analysis (FPCA) plays a central role as a dimension-reduction and representation tool in functional data analysis, but its minimax theory for diverging spectral indices under noisy discrete observation has remained open for over two decades. To fill this gap, we consider a sieve-based FPCA framework that pools discrete measurements across subjects and accommodates sampling frequencies ranging from sparse to dense under random designs. We begin by establishing new minimax rates for covariance estimation over general bivariate function classes beyond tensor-product low-complexity structures, thereby identifying the intrinsically two-dimensional optimal rate. Our central theoretical contribution is to establish minimax optimal rates for both individually labelled eigenfunctions with diverging indices and leading principal subspaces of increasing dimensions, under explicit growth and regularity conditions. To establish these results, we develop a general framework for sharp minimax analysis of FPCA under discrete observation, separating spectral approximation from stochastic perturbations and exploiting their distinct structures, thereby offering a new approach to a broad class of nonparametric spectral estimation problems. For both spectral targets, the optimal rates reveal two distinct statistical mechanisms, spectral identification and nonparametric reconstruction, whose interplay gives rise to either four or two sampling regimes. This yields, for the first time, a precise characterization of the impact of discrete sampling across the full range from sparse to dense designs. Finally, as a downstream application, we analyze FPCA-based functional linear regression and show that the FPCA-based estimator attains the minimax-optimal rates.
core_methodology: Sieve-based Functional Principal Component Analysis (FPCA) for dimension reduction on functional data with discrete measurements
data_sources: General discrete measurements from functional data (not specific to financial data)
alpha_potential: Potential application in analyzing high-dimensional financial time series but requires significant adaptation and domain-specific validation

title: Diffusion Models are Provably Efficient Priors for Sparse Recovery
summary: Diffusion models have transformed generative modeling through their ability to capture and generate samples from complex data distributions. This success has spurred substantial interest in using pretrained diffusion models as expressive priors for highly ill-posed inverse problems in imaging and sensing. Despite strong empirical performance, theoretical understanding of this approach remains limited: existing guarantees are often asymptotic or entail prohibitive computational costs in the worst case. In this paper, we address this gap by studying sparse recovery from a small number of linear measurements, a classical problem in compressed sensing. We show that, given an accurate diffusion model capturing a sparsity-promoting Bernoulli-Gaussian prior, a likelihood-guided annealed Langevin sampler provably recovers the sparse signal in polynomial time with near-optimal sample complexity for a broad family of random and deterministic sensing matrices. When the signal is indeed drawn from the postulated prior, we further establish total variation guarantees for posterior sampling after a final denoising step. These results lay a theoretical foundation for statistically and computationally efficient inverse solvers with diffusion priors.
core_methodology: Uses diffusion models as priors for sparse signal recovery in compressed sensing
data_sources: Theoretical/mathematical models of sparse signals (not market data)
alpha_potential: Potential theoretical foundation for future sparse signal processing in market data, but requires significant adaptation

title: Games played by Exponential Weights Algorithms
summary: This paper studies the last-iterate convergence properties of the exponential weights algorithm with constant learning rates. We consider a repeated interaction in discrete time, where each player uses an exponential weights algorithm characterized by an initial mixed action and a fixed learning rate, so that the mixed action profile $p^t$ played at stage $t$ follows an homogeneous Markov chain. At first, we show that whenever a strict Nash equilibrium exists, the probability to play a strict Nash equilibrium at the next stage converges almost surely to 0 or 1. Secondly, we show that the limit of $p^t$, whenever it exists, belongs to the set of ``Nash Equilibria with Equalizing Payoffs''. Thirdly, we show that in strong coordination games, where the payoff of a player is positive on the diagonal and 0 elsewhere, $p^t$ converges almost surely to one of the strict Nash equilibria. We conclude with open questions.
core_methodology: Exponential weights algorithm with constant learning rates for repeated game interactions
data_sources: Theoretical game theory framework (no market data used)
alpha_potential: Potential applications in understanding strategic interactions in market maker/taker scenarios, but highly theoretical

title: SoK: Market Microstructure for Decentralized Prediction Markets (DePMs)
summary: Decentralized prediction markets (DePMs) allow open participation in event-based wagering without fully relying on centralized intermediaries. We review the history of DePMs which date back to 2011 and includes hundreds of proposals. Perhaps surprising, modern DePMs like Polymarket deviate materially from earlier designs like Truthcoin and Augur v1. We use our review to present a modular workflow comprising eight stages: underlying infrastructure, market topic, share structure and pricing, market initialization, trading, market resolution, settlement, and archiving. For each module, we enumerate the design variants, analyzing trade-offs around decentralization, expressiveness, and manipulation resistance. We also identify open problems for researchers interested in this ecosystem.
core_methodology: Review and modular analysis of decentralized prediction market designs
data_sources: Historical and current decentralized prediction market implementations
alpha_potential: Limited direct alpha potential, but provides insights into market microstructure of alternative trading venues

title: Consecutive Preferential Bayesian Optimization
summary: Preferential Bayesian optimization allows optimization of objectives that are either expensive or difficult to measure directly, by relying on a minimal number of comparative evaluations done by a human expert. Generating candidate solutions for evaluation is also often expensive, but existing preferential optimization methods do not account for this production cost. We introduce Consecutive Preferential Bayesian Optimization (CPBO) for the consecutive setting, where production cost is reduced by reusing the previous candidate in each comparison. We also account for the perceptual ambiguity of the oracle providing the feedback by incorporating a Just-Noticeable Difference threshold into a probabilistic preference model to capture indifference to small utility differences. We adapt an information-theoretic acquisition strategy to this setting, selecting new configurations that are most informative about the unknown optimum under a preference model accounting for the perceptual ambiguity. We empirically demonstrate a notable increase in accuracy in setups with high production costs or indifference feedback, and demonstrate the practical feasibility of CPBO in a real-world food extrusion task.
core_methodology: Bayesian optimization with preference learning and cost-sensitive candidate generation
data_sources: Human expert comparisons (not directly tied to financial data)
alpha_potential: Potential for optimizing expensive-to-evaluate functions in financial contexts, but unclear direct trading application

title: The multiplicative Lipschitz bound as an inductive bias
summary: We study the problem of training a neural network to minimize a loss function given a Lipschitz constraint. While the most obvious way to estimate the Lipschitz constant of a neural network is to multiply the Lipschitz constants of its layers, this bound, which we term the _trivial bound_, is often considered impractically loose. We show that, on the contrary, it can be more effective than state-of-the-art methods (Sandwich, Almost-Orthogonal Layers, Convex Potential Layers, and SDP-based Lipschitz Layers) for Lipschitz-constrained learning. Our method combines the trivial bound with a novel activation function (the quadrature nonlinearity) to achieve lower cross-entropy over most of the tested classification bounds. For autoencoders constrained to be nonexpansive in a learned norm, it achieves the lowest pixel reconstruction error at every tested bottleneck width, improving on PCA by 12--24%. Our architecture, consisting of concatenated cosine and sine activations, is supported by a semi-rigorous theoretical analysis of Lipschitz bound looseness that may prove valuable in its own right.
core_methodology: Training neural networks with Lipschitz constraints using a novel activation function (quadrature nonlinearity) and layer-wise Lipschitz bounds
data_sources: Not specified (likely standard classification/autoencoder datasets)
alpha_potential: Potential for creating more stable/robust models in financial applications, but no direct trading application demonstrated

title: Learning to Decide with AI Assistance under Human-Alignment
summary: It is widely agreed that when AI models assist decision-makers in high-stakes domains by predicting an outcome of interest, they should communicate the confidence of their predictions. However, empirical evidence suggests that decision-makers often struggle to determine when to trust a prediction based solely on this communicated confidence. In this context, recent theoretical and empirical work suggests a positive correlation between the utility of AI-assisted decision-making and the degree of alignment between the AI confidence and the decision-makers' confidence in their own predictions. Crucially, these findings do not yet elucidate the extent to which this alignment influences the complexity of learning to make optimal decisions through repeated interactions. In this paper, we address this question in the canonical case of binary predictions and binary decisions. We first show that this problem is equivalent to a two-armed online contextual learning problem with full feedback, and establish a lower bound of $\Omega (\sqrt{|H| \cdot |B| \cdot T} )$ on the expected regret any learner can attain, where $H$ and $B$ denote the sets of human and AI confidence values. We then demonstrate that, under perfect alignment between AI and human confidence, a learner can attain an expected regret of $O(\sqrt{|H| \cdot T\log T})$ and, when $\sqrt{|H|} = O(\log T)$ and $B$ is countable, a non-trivial generalization of the Dvoretzky-Kiefer-Wolfowitz inequality improves the regret bound to $O(\sqrt{T\log T})$. Taken together, these results reveal that alignment can reduce the complexity of learning to make decisions with AI assistance. Experiments on real data from two different human-subject studies where participants solve simple decision-making tasks assisted by AI models show that our theoretical results are robust to violations of perfect alignment.
core_methodology: The paper studies the problem of learning to make optimal decisions with AI assistance under human-alignment, focusing on binary predictions and decisions. It establishes theoretical bounds on regret in online contextual learning with full feedback.
data_sources: Real data from two different human-subject studies where participants solve simple decision-making tasks assisted by AI models.
alpha_potential: Limited direct alpha potential, but the concept of human-AI alignment in decision-making could be adapted to improve human-AI collaboration in trading decisions.

title: Embedding Foundation Model Predictions in Discrete-Choice Models with Structural Guarantees
summary: Tabular foundation models achieve strong accuracy on choice prediction tasks, but their predictions often violate the economic logic those tasks require: raising a price can increase predicted demand, implied estimates of willingness to pay are frequently negative or implausible, and unavailable alternatives receive nonzero probability. We propose TabFM-Logit, an adapter that takes a foundation model's predicted choice probabilities as a precomputed feature and embeds them inside a multinomial logit's utility. In Stage 1, we fit the multinomial logit's structural coefficients by maximum likelihood with sign constraints. In Stage 2, we freeze those coefficients and fit a small neural correction operating on the foundation model's predictions. We prove that this composition exactly preserves the multinomial logit's marginal rate of substitution, so the analytically computable value of time becomes a mathematical guarantee rather than an empirical accident, and that training the two stages jointly breaks identifiability of the structural coefficients. Counterfactual derivatives and response signs are therefore the multinomial logit's by construction, and the foundation model contributes accuracy on observed choices. On respondents and households unseen in training, the adapter gains 5.7-6.8 percentage points (pp) of test accuracy on Swissmetro, 1.5 pp on LPMC, and 3.3-3.6 pp on IoT-Wearables over the multinomial logit (4.2 pp on average), stays within 1.0 pp of the raw foundation model, maintains 100% cost monotonicity, and keeps the multinomial logit's values of time exactly. The gain is largest where the multinomial logit is weakest and smallest where it is already strong. In every case it comes with the multinomial logit's guarantees, which the raw foundation models lack.
core_methodology: Combines foundation models with multinomial logit to improve choice prediction while maintaining economic logic
data_sources: Non-financial datasets (Swissmetro, LPMC, IoT-Wearables)
alpha_potential: Limited direct applications - methodology could theoretically be adapted for discrete choices in trading contexts

title: Reinforcement Learning for Large-Scale Lifelong Multi-Agent Path Finding with Shared Spatial Fields
summary: Large-scale applications of lifelong multi-agent path finding (LMAPF) call for computationally inexpensive movement decisions under changing traffic conditions and across varied layouts. We propose a navigation policy in which a convolutional network computes a shared spatial field over the map once per timestep and a compact goal-conditioned operator derives agents' movement preferences. The complete policy is trained end-to-end using average-reward reinforcement learning with throughput as the reward, without planner demonstrations or a separate online path planner. For structured and unstructured layouts, we train one policy per class on pools of small maps and deploy each without retraining on larger, unseen layouts and agent populations. Across six layouts with 10,000 agents, our policies achieve throughput comparable to or higher than the strongest evaluated baselines. The proposed method has an average execution time below 10 ms per step, more than an order of magnitude faster than several established planners.
core_methodology: Reinforcement learning for multi-agent path finding with shared spatial fields
data_sources: Simulated spatial environments and agent movement data
alpha_potential: Potential applications in optimizing trade execution in dark pools or similar multi-agent trading systems

title: TGTV: Interpretable Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection in UAV Telemetry
summary: Anomaly detection in multivariate fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) telemetry is complicated by operating-condition transitions, asynchronous sensor sampling, and control-system compensation that can obscure fault signatures. Existing temporal detection methods have limited capacity to represent coupled faults across subsystems, track their evolution, and constrain language-model diagnoses with quantitative evidence. This paper proposes TGTV, an interpretable framework for multivariate telemetry anomaly detection and traceable fault analysis that integrates spatiotemporal graph learning with a large language model. A temporal convolutional network and a graph attention network with weighted fused adjacency extract multiscale temporal patterns and spatial dependencies among sensors. A hybrid temporal Transformer and variational autoencoder then evaluates window-level anomalies using prediction errors and reconstruction probabilities. Continuous-time Shapley attribution identifies critical sensors and high-contribution intervals while preserving the temporal continuity of fault evolution. A structured evidence package combines detection results, graph relationships, temporal attribution, sensor attribution, and operating context. An evidence-constrained diagnosis protocol uses this package to generate flight-level conclusions with traceable evidence identifiers. Cross-flight holdout experiments on the public ALFA fixed-wing flight dataset yield a window-level area under the precision-recall curve of 0.976, accuracy of 0.973, recall of 0.902, and F1 score of 0.920. Flight-level fault diagnosis achieves recall of 0.943 and an F1 score of 0.944. These results demonstrate accurate anomaly detection and quantitatively supported fault-tracing cues, providing a basis for interpretable post-flight fault review and analysis.
core_methodology: The paper proposes TGTV, a framework combining spatiotemporal graph learning with a large language model for multivariate telemetry anomaly detection, using temporal convolutional networks, graph attention networks, and hybrid Transformer-VAE models.
data_sources: Public ALFA fixed-wing flight dataset containing UAV telemetry data.
alpha_potential: Limited direct applicability to financial markets, but the methodology for anomaly detection in multivariate time-series could be adapted for detecting anomalies in high-frequency trading data or market microstructure analysis.

title: Probabilistic State Space Enumeration in Neural Network Computation
summary: Many methods for pruning neural networks rank weights or groups of weights by importance and retain a single subset. We study how channel groups contribute jointly to the output of multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) in Transformer language models. Inspired by network reliability analysis, probabilistic state space enumeration (PSSE) represents the dense MLP output as the expected importance-corrected masked output over $2^G$ joint states of $G$ channel groups. Summing the most probable states' probability-weighted outputs gives an approximation whose absolute error is bounded by the omitted probability mass times the maximum masked-output norm. NORDER-II adapts ORDER-II to enumerate states in decreasing probability without sorting the full space. Its first $B$ states maximize the probability mass captured at that budget. A weight-entropy scorer fixes each layer's ordering from pretrained weights. We evaluate all 168 MLP layers across six models from the Llama, Gemma, and Qwen families on two datasets with 8, 16, and 32 channel groups. In all 1,008 comparisons, the 95%-mass prefix yields lower mean relative error than uniform sampling at the same state count, with or without bias correction.
